item.title: At least one Lebanese person, two Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon
item.description: The violence comes amid talks between Lebanon and Israel as Beirut pushes for a phased Israeli troop withdrawal.

item.title: LIV Golf secures ‘lead’ investor for player-driven future after Saudi exit
item.description: An agreement with an unnamed investor is approved by the LIV Golf board to replace Saudi Arabia deal.

item.title: Russia kills 17 in ballistic missile attacks around Kyiv
item.description: At least 17 people were killed after Russia launched an overnight ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV to visit Peru, Argentina and Uruguay in November
item.description: The pontiff’s first Latin America trip will take him back to Peru, where he spent decades as a missionary and bishop.

item.title: Puerto Rican cities hit with water rationing measures during record drought
item.description: Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez says she does not know how long the rationing measures will remain in place.

item.title: Arab officials call for action over Jerusalem tensions
item.description: Arab officials call for action over Jerusalem tensions

item.title: Top Arab, Muslim diplomats launch plan to protect Jerusalem religious sites
item.description: Foreign ministers warn Christian and Islamic holy sites 'threatened' by Israel 'as never before'.

item.title: UK tribunal confirms professor’s anti-Zionism is legally protected belief
item.description: David Miller has told Al Jazeera the ruling is a victory that will encourage others to speak out against Zionism.

item.title: War on Iran: US-Iran deal edges closer
item.description: A deal between the US and Iran could be signed within 48 hours, according to US officials.

item.title: Germany investigates explosive device attached to drone at Leipzig airport
item.description: An airport employee spotted the object carrying what authorities described as 'an unknown explosive device'.

item.title: Demolition complicates the search for bodies after Venezuela’s earthquakes
item.description: Venezuela has begun tearing down unstable buildings after its deadly earthquakes. But what is the cost to survivors?

item.title: Gaza father opens play center to restore childhood amid Israeli attacks
item.description: A Palestinian father opened a Gaza play center offering children free escape and joy amid near daily Israeli attacks.

item.title: Boxer Chapman recovering after emergency surgery for brain bleed
item.description: Featherweight Raven Chapman collapsed while sparring on July 24 and was rushed to surgery, her team says.

item.title: Ex-PM Sheikh Hasina announces plan to return to Bangladesh
item.description: The decision of the 78-year-old ousted leader comes despite her facing the death penalty in Bangladesh.

item.title: Why are US Republicans losing faith in War Secretary Pete Hegseth?
item.description: The reasons for dissent are not unanimous, ranging from the war in Iran to an overhaul of military leadership.

item.title: Iraq faces crisis as Shia armed groups defy disarmament
item.description: Iraqi PM faces a serious crisis as powerful Shia paramilitaries refuse to disarm as September 30 deadline looms.

item.title: Former heavyweight champ ⁠Parker cleared to fight again after doping ban
item.description: Joseph Parker was suspended in October after failing a voluntary drug test, but denied taking any prohibited substance.

item.title: UN rights chief says Iran executed at least 56 people since March
item.description: Volker Turk warns of surge in Iran executions to suppress dissent after January uprising.

item.title: Pakistan’s Khan in jail for 3 years: PTI rallies over ‘arbitrary detention’
item.description: Thousands of supporters of former PM Imran Khan's party demonstrate across country to call for his immediate release.

item.title: SpaceX rocket segment to crash into the moon: What happened?
item.description: A piece of the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket is believed to have crashed into the moon after floating in space since last year.

item.title: Mohamed Salah lands in Turkiye to fan frenzy ahead of Trabzonspor move
item.description: Mohamed Salah lands in Turkiye to fan frenzy ahead of Trabzonspor move.

item.title: In Bandar Abbas, the ceasefire never came
item.description: A single mother from Bandar Abbas reflects on the fear and resilience of living through repeated attacks.

item.title: Iran, Oman, US ‘close’ to Hormuz deal: What do they all want?
item.description: An agreement could restore shipping through crucial waterway, paving way for peace talks between Tehran and Washington.

item.title: Protesters stage sit-in against settler violence-linked Smotrich funds
item.description: Palestinian and Israeli protesters staged a sit-in at the Religious Zionist Party’s headquarters in Shoham on Wednesday.

item.title: Turkish cargo ship catches fire after Black Sea drone attack
item.description: A Turkish cargo ship caught fire after a drone attack near Russia’s Black Sea port of Novorossiysk.
